Lunigiana is a wild territory wedged between three regions (Tuscany, Liguria and Emilia-Romagna), where the Via Francigena crosses chestnut forests, crystal-clear rivers, perched castles and medieval villages that seem frozen in time.

The Apennine mountains merge with the Apuan Alps, offering breathtaking panoramas. And yet you're not isolated, since within an hour's drive you can reach eight provincial capitals.

È ottobre del 2020, il mondo è ancora fr: It's October 2020 and the world is still reeling from the pandemic; remote work has become everyday life for a great many people. The inland areas and small villages of the Apennines have been losing their people for years. Two young people from Pontremoli ask themselves a question: how can we bring people back here? And so an idea is born: if Pontremoli can't offer work, work will come to Pontremoli.
Tutto è cominciato con un sito, tanto pa: It all started with a website, a lot of word of mouth and the determination of people with a dream who believe in it. From the start the project had the backing of the Municipality of Pontremoli, the Lions Club Pontremoli Lunigiana and the Rotary Club Lunigiana. The first people arrived, and soon we were flooded with requests from all over the world: some are still here, and Lunigiana has become their home. In August 2023 the community became an association, Start Working Pontremoli APS.

In Lunigiana lo sport e la natura si fon: In Lunigiana sport and nature blend into a unique experience in every season. The gyms and yoga studios nearby are perfect for training indoors, but the real magic of the area is in the surrounding nature.
Le valli della Lunigiana, con i loro sen: Lunigiana's valleys, with their centuries-old paths, invite you to explore breathtaking landscapes of woods and Apennine ridges. The thrill of river trekking in the Stretti di Giaredo, where the water has carved spectacular canyons, alternates with mountain bike trails between old villages and medieval castles.
Qui ogni escursione diventa un'avventura: Here every outing becomes an adventure: from the gentle paths along the Magra river to the climbs towards Monte Molinatico, always with the Apuan Alps on the horizon.
La magia di Pontremoli e della Lunigiana: The magic of Pontremoli and Lunigiana lives in its events, which turn the villages into a stage for centuries-old traditions and celebration. They're not just events, but moments when the community gathers and tells its story.
I falò di Pontremoli sono la manifestazi: Pontremoli's bonfires are the most spectacular winter event in Lunigiana: huge fires tied to ancient traditions are built along the beds of the Magra and Verde rivers and burned in honour of San Nicolò (17 January) and San Geminiano (31 January).
Ogni agosto celebra il diploma di Libero: Every August it celebrates the free-commune charter granted to Pontremoli by Emperor Frederick II in 1226, who called the town «clavis et ianua», key and gateway between Lombardy and Tuscany. Thanks to the Compagnia del Piagnaro, for five days the town turns medieval: no cars in the centre, only travellers, merchants, carriages and knights.
Due volte l'anno questo giro enogastrono: Twice a year this food-and-wine tour in stages fills the town with a celebration of traditional flavours. The record is 1,387 participants, competing over testaroli, Amor and Bianco Oro.
Ogni agosto dal 1983, nel cuore medieval: Every August since 1983, in the medieval heart of Mulazzo, Bancarel'Vino celebrates Lunigiana's wine tradition: a wine competition, tastings and cultural events turn the village for three days into a meeting point for experts and enthusiasts.

On a Thursday evening a guest presents a topic, a trip or a hobby, and we talk, swap ideas and have a beer together, at the Birreria del Moro, with beers and focaccine.
